newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-TAPANI SHINES IN CUBS DEBUT AGAINST BRAVES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-TAPANI SHINES IN CUBS DEBUT AGAINST BRAVES.

text.p: The Chicago Cubs will have gotten a bargain if Kevin Tapani, who signed a three-year, $11 million contract in the offseason, is as good as he was in his debut for them Wednesday.
Tapani, coming back after surgery, allowed only one run in seven-plus innings with nine strikeouts to help the Cubs to a 3-1 victory over the National League-leading Atlanta Braves.

Tapani (1-0) gave up five hits and did not walk a batter while falling one short of his career best strikeout total. After allowing a homer to Danny Bautista and a single to Mark Lemke leading off the eighth, Tapani gave way to four relievers, with Mel Rojas finishing for his 13th save.

Tapani left the White Sox to sign a three-year, $11 million contract with the Cubs in the offseason, but his debut on the north side of the city was delayed after surgery on April 4. The 33-year-old had scar tissue removed from the ulnar collateral ligament in his right index finger.
"Obviously, the expectations were great today for me, but I wasn't sure what to expect from myself," Tapanmi admitted.

"I think that all my pitches were working pretty well and the fact that the Braves haven't seen me for a long time certainly helped as well. I'm not the type of guy that will go out and strike out a lot of people. But I had really good control of all my pitches today."
Sammy Sosa had a pair of hits and two RBI, including his 19th homer of the season, a solo shot in the eighth that gave the bullpen some breathing room.
Rookie Kevin Millwood (1-2) took the loss.

In Los Angeles, Brian Bohanon came up from the minors and combined with three relievers on a four-hitter and Manny Alexander scored both New York runs as the Mets held on for a 2-1 victory over the Dodgers.

Bohanon (2-1) was recalled from Triple-A Norfolk and started in place of the injured Armando Reynoso. He gave up four hits, including a solo homer to Tom Prince, walked two and struck out three. He is 2-0 in as many starts this season.

Cory Lidle retired all six batters he faced, running his scoreless streak to 7 2/3 innings over eight appearances. Greg McMichael breezed through the eighth and John Franco worked the ninth for his 26th save in 30 chances.
The Mets have won six of their last seven games and are 12-6 in their last 18 one-run games. They won in Los Angeles for just the second time in eight contests.
Dennis Reyes (1-2) took the loss.
In San Diego, Pete Smith scattered five hits over seven innings and Tony Gwynn had two hits and three RBI as the Padres routed the Pittsburgh Pirates 9-1.
Smith (4-1), who has won all three of his starts this season, allowed one run in his longest outing of the year.
Gwynn had an RBI single in the first inning and a two-run double in the second before he was removed in the third with tightness in his left hamstring.
The Padres posted their fourth straight win.
Jon Lieber (6-10) was tagged for six runs and six hits in 1 1/3 innings, his shortest outing of the season.
In Cincinnati, Bobby Bonilla and Charles Johnson homered in a five-run sixth, powering the Florida Marlins past the Reds 8-1 to snap a three-game hitting streak.

Alex Fernandez (11-8) gave up one run and six hits with five strikeouts and three walks in a 140-pitch effort. He carried a shutout into the eighth before Reggie Sanders led off with a homer, his third in two games.
Mike Morgan (3-8) surrendered five runs and six hits over 5 1/3 innings to lose his third straight start. Cincinnati has lost five of its last six games.
In San Francisco, Barry Bonds' grand slam highlighted a seven-run third inning as the Giants scored all of their runs in the first four frames and cruised to a 16-4 rout of the Philadelphia Phillies.
It was Bonds' 360th career homer, putting him in 44th place on the all-time list, one behind Joe DiMaggio.

Philadelphia starter Mark Leiter (5-11) allowed nine runs -- five earned -- and seven hits with four walks in 2 2/3 innings. Shawn Estes (13-4) got the win, yielding four runs -- three earned -- over five innings.
J.T. Snow had two hits while Bill Mueller was 4-for-4 with a two-run homer and a career-high five RBI for the Giants.

In St. Louis, Thomas Howard hit a two-run homer and added an RBI triple and Mike Magnante pitched 3 2/3 innings of perfect relief as the Houston Astros defeated the Cardinals 7-2 for their fifth straight victory.
Howard's homer in the top of the first off Todd Stottlemyre (9-7) staked the Astros to a 2-0 lead. Howard finished 3-for-4.
Magnante (3-0) struck out two to get the victory for Houston, which has won seven straight on the road and eight of nine overall.
